steps.say: Tides is the macro layer: the big money flows behind every chart. | Rates, the dollar, inflation, fear, credit, and where money is rotating. | They move slowly, but they set the conditions every asset trades in.
The Tide sums up twelve currents. | Coming in means risk-supportive. Slack means mixed. Going out means risk-defensive. | A new Tide only counts after five daily closes.
The Sea state is how rough the water is: calm, moderate, rough, or storm. | That's low to extreme volatility, from the VIX and Bitcoin.
The winds apply the currents to each market. | A tailwind helps longs in that market. A headwind works against them.
The calendar flags the big scheduled releases: the Fed, inflation, and jobs. | A storm warning means an event is near. It isn't a forecast.
The waves draw each current over time, with the swell they make together. | Dashed lines mark past Fed, inflation and jobs days.
Each current is scored against its own last five years, from very low to very high. | Its pull says whether it's rising, falling, or flat, and which way that pushes risk.
Beside the daily note, the AI Navigator answers questions about these readings. | Today's AI Passage Plan applies them to your own assets and funnels.
The plan covers the conditions, the week's events, the winds for your assets, the hazards, and things to watch. | One plan a day, kept in your logbook.
Macro conditions frame risk over weeks. | They don't time trades, and a coin can rise on its own news while the tide goes out.
